 Issued: 27 July 2026, JRC MARS Bulletin Vol. 34 No. 6   JRC MARS Bulletin 
Crop monitoring in Europe – July 2026 Exceptional winter crop yields confirmed in Türkiye 
Repeated heatwaves shortened the grain-
filling phase of winter crops and brought 
forward the harvest, which has already been 
completed in the south and is progressing 
elsewhere. EU yield forecasts for winter crops 
have been revised downwards by 1–4 %, 
leaving the outlook for total cereals at 1 % 
below the five-year average. 
For summer crops, exceptional heat and 
limited rainfall across western and central 
Europe depleted soil moisture, constrained 
biomass accumulation and affected flowering. 
Yield forecasts have been reduced for all 
spring and summer crops, most notably for 
grain maize and sunflowers (6–7 %). Hot and 
dry conditions are forecast to persist in 
western Europe, increasing the likelihood of 
further yield reductions. 
This edition includes an extended analysis of 
Türkiye, where a cool, wet spring supported 
record-high winter crop yields and favourable 
prospects for summer crops.
